npcs.name: Nell Riverwick
npcs.description: A street sweep rooted at market lanes at dawn, known for how she listens more than she sweeps.
npcs.biography: Nell did not plan to become the neighborhood's go-to street sweep, yet market lanes at dawn made the choice stick. Now 24, the Human measures success in quiet evenings and unpaid favors returned. She listens more than she sweeps, and keeps the pocket full of lost buttons she means to return the way a confessor keeps secrets. Friend to Finn; informant to Merrick. Hope pulls one way—save for a room that doesn't leak—while caution pulls the other because of being noticed by the wrong people for noticing too much. Mapped which cellar grates glow after midnight for Merrick.
npcs.personality: Steady and sharp-eyed; listens more than she sweeps.
npcs.motivation: To save for a room that doesn't leak, even while fearing being noticed by the wrong people for noticing too much.
npcs.secret: Knows more about this than she admits: Mapped which cellar grates glow after midnight for Merrick.
npcs.rumor: A smugglers' mark was seen near market lanes at dawn on a night Nell worked late.
npcs.voice: Low and practical, with a habit of repeating the important clause once.
npcs.appearance: A human silhouette framed by market lanes at dawn, hands seldom empty of the pocket full of lost buttons she means to return.

relationships.note: Passes street details for tea money.

npcs.name: Jab Millroad
npcs.description: Jab holds down warehouse yards and wagon rows with callused competence and open ears.
npcs.biography: Walk into warehouse yards and wagon rows and you will find Jab Millroad before you find a free chair. A 38-year-old Human carter, Jab greets trouble the way other folk greet weather: with a coat and a plan. He names his mules after bad decisions. The waybill clipboard chewed at the corners travels with him almost everywhere. Hauls for Garr; drinks with Old Tallow. His ambition is to buy a covered wagon before winter rain. His nightmare is highway 'tolls' that aren't official. Right now, Was paid double to deliver an unmarked crate to the an abandoned mill and ask nothing.
npcs.personality: Warm with regulars, curt with wasters; names his mules after bad decisions.
npcs.motivation: Secure enough ground to buy a covered wagon before winter rain.
npcs.secret: Quietly arranging matters around this problem: Was paid double to deliver an unmarked crate to the an abandoned mill and ask nothing.
npcs.rumor: Jab is said to keep a private list of debts local officials will not touch.
npcs.voice: Polite public voice; sharper private asides when trust appears.
npcs.appearance: Looks like someone who sleeps lightly; distinctive detail is the waybill clipboard chewed at the corners.

npcs.name: Oma Kettle
npcs.description: A laundry worker rooted at wash lines behind town houses, known for how she hums lullabies to stained sheets.
npcs.biography: Oma learned the hard corners of settlement life by working them as a laundry worker based out of wash lines behind town houses. At 70, the Halfling has a map of loyalties written in calluses rather than ink. Day after day she hums lullabies to stained sheets, and the cake of soap scented with river mint marks her place in the room. Washes for manor staff; knows Ora. Her north star is to see her grandson apprenticed cleanly. The shadow at her heels is illness spreading through shared basins. Found a blood-stiffened shirt with a Vale-colored thread in the cuff.

npcs.name: Finn Cobble
npcs.description: Familiar face at doorsteps across town; useful, stubborn, and hard to surprise.
npcs.biography: Finn learned the hard corners of settlement life by working them as a messenger boy based out of doorsteps across town. At 16, the Human has a map of loyalties written in calluses rather than ink. Day after day he runs messages before he reads them—usually, and the scuffed satchel with a false seam marks his place in the room. Idolizes Blink; friends with Nell. His north star is to become a long-road courier like Blink. The shadow at his heels is delivering something that gets a friend hanged. Peeked at a letter from Brother Caldus naming Magister Quen.

npcs.name: Bera Wells
npcs.description: The well keeper people recommend when they actually want the job finished.
npcs.biography: Some locals swear Bera was born mid-shift at the public well; the truth is only slightly less devoted. This human well keeper, now 52, treats competence like courtesy. She rations buckets fairly when drought talk starts, never far from the iron well key on a red cord. Community voice; speaks to Mayor Haldrin. Ask what she wants and she names it plainly: fund a second well before the next dry summer. Ask what she dreads and the answer is poison or panic at the water. Then comes the fresh problem—Noticed a bitter taste the morning after smugglers used the mill race.
npcs.personality: Soft-spoken until principles are poked; rations buckets fairly when drought talk starts.
npcs.motivation: Turn today's scrapes into tomorrow's chance to fund a second well before the next dry summer.
npcs.secret: Night thoughts keep returning to poison or panic at the water, especially since: Noticed a bitter taste the morning after smugglers used the mill race.
npcs.rumor: Someone paid Bera to forget a name connected to recent trouble near the public well.
npcs.voice: Quick local diction, then sudden silences that mean more than words.
npcs.appearance: Easy to spot near the public well: human, practical layers, and the iron well key on a red cord.

Her north star is to train one apprentice who isn't afraid of heights. The shadow at her heels is falling through a rotten stack. Saw signal lanterns answering each other from mill to river from a roof ridge.

npcs.name: Mael Ferry
npcs.description: Local dock hauler whose days orbit the docks and small lasting loyalties.
npcs.biography: Before dawn, Mael is already at the docks, working as a dock hauler with yesterday's work still on his fingers. The habit everyone notices is simple: he rolls shoulders before lifting anything proud. Close by sits his prized the hooks and gloves stiff with river salt, a small anchor in a loud settlement. Works near Tem Brine; wary of Nedda. He wants to join a river crew with proper shares. He fears cranes failing on a crowded quay more than open confrontation. A useful adventure hook trails him: Helped Nedda unload 'grain' that smelled of lamp oil.
npcs.personality: Dry humor over a careful heart; rolls shoulders before lifting anything proud.
npcs.motivation: Finish one honest plan: join a river crew with proper shares.
npcs.secret: Keeps proof related to a problem—Helped Nedda unload 'grain' that smelled of lamp oil.
npcs.rumor: Locals whisper that the hooks and gloves stiff with river salt once belonged to a traveler who vanished on the road.
npcs.voice: Storyteller rhythm even when discussing ledgers or latches.
npcs.appearance: Human features shaped by work at the docks; watch for the hooks and gloves stiff with river salt.

npcs.name: Yara Moss
npcs.description: Local herb gatherer whose days orbit roadside hedges and garden edges and small lasting loyalties.
npcs.biography: Yara Moss works from roadside hedges and garden edges with the stubborn patience of a 26-year-old Half-Elf who has already survived harder seasons. She thanks plants before she cuts them, and keeps the drying racks of labeled leaves close when tempers rise. Supplies Petra; walks trails with Kavi. Her private aim is simple: publish a simple herbal for midwives. Still, she flinches at the thought of overharvesting a rare feverwort patch. Lately a fresh problem has landed in her lap: Found bootprints and chalk arrows near her feverwort—heading toward the mill.
